query: High-entropy alloys contain five or more elements at 5–35 at% each, generally with comparable atomic radii. Refractory and nickel-based high-entropy alloys have demonstrated elevated-temperature mechanical properties comparable to titanium- and nickel-based alloys used in extreme environments because of their heat resistance and specific strength. However, prior investigations have mainly treated titanium and nickel as additions, leaving alloys in which both are primary constituents unexplored. Subject to the stated compositional definition, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted relative outcome, composition and operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled amount of tungsten into the titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy will lead to in situ formation of fine tungsten‐rich precipitates that hinder dislocation motion at elevated temperatures, thereby improving its high-temperature mechanical strength relative to the same alloy without tungsten.
generation.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy with five or more elements meeting the 5–35 at% criterion and with titanium and nickel as the primary constituents, produced by standard casting or melting routes.
generation.intervention: Doping the baseline titanium–nickel high-entropy alloy with a minor amount of tungsten (for example, on the order of a few atomic percent added during alloy synthesis) to promote precipitation of tungsten‐rich phases.
generation.conditions: Both the baseline and tungsten-doped alloys are synthesized under identical processing conditions. The evaluation is performed via standard high-temperature mechanical tests (for instance, tensile or creep tests) at elevated temperatures typical of refractory or nickel-based superalloys. All testing variables (temperature, strain rate, environment) are held constant.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of fine, tungsten-enriched precipitates dispersed within the alloy matrix.
generation.mechanism: Precipitation strengthening: The tungsten-rich precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion under high-temperature loading, thereby increasing yield and ultimate tensile strength and enhancing creep resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The tungsten-doped alloy is predicted to exhibit improved elevated-temperature strength (e.g., higher yield strength and creep resistance) relative to the baseline alloy without tungsten.
generation.baseline: Titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy without tungsten addition.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to alloys that maintain the high-entropy alloy compositional criteria (at least 5 elements with 5–35 at% each) and are evaluated under the same high-temperature mechanical testing conditions as used for current refractory or nickel-based alloys.
generation.uncertainty: The precise concentration of tungsten needed for optimal precipitation and the exact magnitude of the improvement in mechanical performance remain to be determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloy batches: one baseline titanium–nickel high-entropy alloy and one alloy doped with the chosen tungsten concentration. Process both alloys under identical conditions and then subject them to high-temperature mechanical tests (such as tensile tests at defined elevated temperatures or creep tests under controlled strain rates).
measurements: Yield strength at the test temperature
Creep strain or creep rate under defined stress conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tungsten-doped alloy does not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in the measured elevated-temperature mechanical properties (e.g., higher yield strength or reduced creep rate) compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
